After this year, Potter's art and writing decreased due to farm management and caring for parents
Beatrix Potter married William Heelis; The Tale of Pigling Bland published

trueFalse.statement: The Tale of Tom Kitten is similar to The Tale of Peter Rabbit because disobedient children lose their clothing.
trueFalse.correction: In both stories the disobedient 'child/ren' lose their clothing which upsets their mothers.

trueFalse.statement: Mrs. Cannon found a rat eating dinner under the kitchen table at Hill Top in the afternoon.
trueFalse.correction: Although Hill Top's rat infestation was mostly unpleasant, this was a humorous sight.

trueFalse.statement: The Tale of Samuel Whiskers and The Tale of Tom Kitten are both set indoors at Hill Top Farm.
trueFalse.correction: Tom Kitten is set outside in the garden and farmyard, while Samuel Whiskers is a tribute to the house interior.

trueFalse.statement: The Tale of Samuel Whiskers was personal to Potter because it celebrated her independence and Hill Top renovations.
trueFalse.correction: It was immensely personal as she had become entirely independent of parents and it celebrates making Hill Top her dream home.

trueFalse.statement: Jemima Puddle-Duck was named after the ornithological illustrator Jemima Blackburn.
trueFalse.correction: This is the likely origin of the character's name according to the study guide.

trueFalse.statement: The Tale of Jemima Puddle-Duck has a happy ending where all the eggs hatch safely.
trueFalse.correction: Although Jemima and eggs are saved by Kep the Collie, the two farm pups eat all of Jemima's eggs.

trueFalse.statement: Potter created both a watercolor painting and a clay figure of her beloved collie Kep.
trueFalse.correction: She used multiple mediums to capture her favorite farm dog.

trueFalse.statement: Potter eagerly sold her two farm pigs because she didn't like them.
trueFalse.correction: Although saddened by the event, she was accepting because she was paid well and they ate so much it was difficult to keep them fed.

trueFalse.statement: The imagery in The Tale of Mrs. Tittlemouse harkened back to Potter's early natural history illustrations.
trueFalse.correction: This story connected to her detailed scientific observation work from earlier years.

trueFalse.statement: Warne encouraged Potter to include as many different creatures as possible in The Tale of Mrs. Tittlemouse.
trueFalse.correction: He had to rein in her enthusiasm - the earwig turned to a beetle, centipede to a butterfly, and woodlice wording changed.

trueFalse.statement: The Tale of Mr. Tod is set in Bull Banks, the pastures of Castle Farm near Near Sawrey.
trueFalse.correction: Specifically underneath Oatmeal Crag in the Near Sawrey countryside.

trueFalse.statement: The Tale of Mr. Tod ends with all disagreements resolved happily.
trueFalse.correction: The tale ends with disagreements unsolved and no resolution between the characters.

trueFalse.statement: Canon Rawnsley gave Potter her first Herdwick sheep.
trueFalse.correction: These sheep have dainty feet and unique wool suitable for cold temperatures and uneven terrain.

trueFalse.statement: Potter began working on The Fairy Caravan again after meeting American visitors who appreciated her story settings.
trueFalse.correction: After meeting Gail Parsons Coolidge and Henry P., who wished to see the real-life settings, she returned to this book.

trueFalse.statement: Johnny Town-Mouse and Timmy Willie both live in Hawkshead.
trueFalse.correction: Johnny Town-Mouse lives in Hawkshead, while Timmy Willie lives in a garden at a cottage in Near Sawrey.

trueFalse.statement: Norman Warne died during the Potter family's stay at Hafod-Y-Bryn in summer 1905.
trueFalse.correction: He had proposed to Beatrix that same summer, making his death particularly tragic.

trueFalse.statement: The Tale of Timmy Tiptoes is considered one of Potter's most pleasing stories.
trueFalse.correction: It's considered one of the least pleasing, proving Potter was best in places that inspired her with creatures she knew well.

trueFalse.statement: Potter wrote to Millie Warne after Norman's death and included a sketch of barley fields.
trueFalse.correction: She included a sketch of the barley fields she painted the night before Norman died.

trueFalse.statement: Benjamin and Flopsy Bunny put toy bunnies in place of their babies when rescuing them from Mr. McGregor.
trueFalse.correction: They put old vegetables and brush from the rubbish heap in the sack in place of their baby bunnies.

trueFalse.statement: Eleanor Taylor believes Potter spoke directly to children without condescension in her books.
trueFalse.correction: This fellow illustrator wrote about this quality in the Afterword of the book.

quiz.question: How is The Tale of Tom Kitten similar to The Tale of Peter Rabbit?
options: Disobedient children lose their clothing which upsets their mothers
Both have cats as main characters
quiz.correctAnswer: Disobedient children lose their clothing which upsets their mothers

quiz.question: What real-life streets in Near Sawrey appear in illustrations?
quiz.correctAnswer: Stoney Lane and Bank Wood

quiz.question: What humorous sight did Mrs. Cannon see during Hill Top's rat infestation?
options: A rat sitting up eating its dinner under the kitchen table in the afternoon
A rat wearing a tiny hat
A rat sleeping in a teacup
quiz.correctAnswer: A rat sitting up eating its dinner under the kitchen table in the afternoon

quiz.question: How do the settings differ between The Tale of Samuel Whiskers and The Tale of Tom Kitten?
options: Tom Kitten is set outside in garden and farmyard; Samuel Whiskers is a tribute to the house
Tom Kitten is inside; Samuel Whiskers is outside
quiz.correctAnswer: Tom Kitten is set outside in garden and farmyard; Samuel Whiskers is a tribute to the house

quiz.question: Why was The Tale of Samuel Whiskers so personal to Beatrix Potter?
options: It celebrated her independence from parents and making Hill Top her dream home
It was her first published book
quiz.correctAnswer: It celebrated her independence from parents and making Hill Top her dream home

quiz.question: Who was Jemima Puddle-Duck likely named after?
options: A character from a fairy tale
quiz.correctAnswer: The ornithological illustrator Jemima Blackburn

quiz.question: What sad ending concludes The Tale of Jemima Puddle-Duck?
options: The two farm pups eat Jemima's eggs
quiz.correctAnswer: The two farm pups eat Jemima's eggs

quiz.question: What other medium besides painting did Beatrix use to create Kep the collie?
quiz.correctAnswer: A clay figure

quiz.question: Why was Beatrix accepting of selling two farm pigs despite being sad?
options: She was paid a good price and they ate so much it was difficult to keep them fed
Her parents made her sell them
quiz.correctAnswer: She was paid a good price and they ate so much it was difficult to keep them fed

quiz.question: What did Beatrix Potter adopt that lived at Hill Top Farm, much to John Cannon's dismay?
quiz.correctAnswer: A little black piglet

quiz.question: Which home acted as a model for Mr. Piperson's house in The Tale of Pigling Bland?
quiz.correctAnswer: The Spout House

quiz.question: What did Potter's imagery in The Tale of Mrs. Tittlemouse harken back to?
quiz.correctAnswer: Her early natural history illustrations

quiz.question: What does Mrs. Tittlemouse give Mr. Jackson through the window?
quiz.correctAnswer: An acorn-cupful of honey-dew

quiz.question: What did Warne have to do with Potter's enthusiasm for creature variety in Mrs. Tittlemouse?

He encouraged her to add more
quiz.correctAnswer: He had to rein in her enthusiasm and some creatures were changed or removed

quiz.question: What is the setting for The Tale of Mr. Tod?
options: Near Sawrey countryside in Bull Banks, pastures of Castle Farm, underneath Oatmeal Crag
quiz.correctAnswer: Near Sawrey countryside in Bull Banks, pastures of Castle Farm, underneath Oatmeal Crag

quiz.question: Why did Potter believe The Tale of Mr. Tod would make a good book?
options: It would make pretty pictures with effects of moonlight
It was set in her favorite location
quiz.correctAnswer: It would make pretty pictures with effects of moonlight

quiz.question: How did The Tale of Mr. Tod end?
options: Disagreements were not solved and there was no resolution
quiz.correctAnswer: Disagreements were not solved and there was no resolution

quiz.question: What makes Herdwick sheep different from most sheep breeds?

quiz.question: Who gave Beatrix Potter her first Herdwick sheep?
quiz.correctAnswer: Canon Rawnsley

quiz.question: What book did Potter begin working on again after meeting Gail Parsons Coolidge and Henry P.?

quiz.question: What is the horse character's name in the unfinished painting of The Fairy Caravan?
